chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abi Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: My father narrated to me, from his grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in what he taught his companions: The gates of the heavens open at five appointed times: at the time of the descent of rain, at the time of marching (for battle), at the time of the call to prayer, at the time of reading the Quran, with the disappearance of the sun, and at the time of the rising of the dawn.
ai.seo_question: What are the five times when the gates of heaven open according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies five pivotal moments when divine mercy descends, linking spiritual acts like Quran recitation and Adhan with natural phenomena like rain and solar transitions. This teaching underscores the Shia understanding of *barakah* (blessing) permeating both the physical and metaphysical realms, encouraging believers to maximize worship during these auspicious windows. The inclusion of 'Zahf' (military march) highlights the intersection of spiritual devotion and communal struggle in early Islamic history.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-80 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather Al-Hassan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB)

that from amongst what the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) taught his companions, he (MGB) said, “The gates of the heavens open at five appointed times. At the time of descending of rain; at the time of a holy war; at the time of the general call to prayer; at the time of reading of the Quran; at the time of the disappearance of the sun and at the time of the rise of the dawn.”
